rows.why: Item 9 asks what unit and default the share uses. Its pick, integer basis points with a default of 7500, gives a release of 7500 on a bounty of 10000. No item covers the 'partially released' status.

Item 1 asks how the share is rounded. Its pick rounds down with BigInt integer division and gives the leftover to UAT, so 999 splits into 749 and 250. BigInt keeps the amounts exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
Item 10 asks how much UAT approval releases. Its pick, the bounty minus all prior releases, is the remaining balance.
Item 4 asks what a failed run does to stored state. Its pick never calls store.set, so nothing is recorded and the task stays locked.
Item 2 asks what happens when UAT is approved before the hidden tests pass. Its pick throws and records nothing, which matches. The pick does not give the error's wording.
Item 7 asks what a bounty of 0 does. Its pick reports 'pro bono' but still records zero-amount releases. The scenario says no release is ever recorded.

Item 5 asks how repeated events are handled. Its pick treats an event as a duplicate when a release of that kind already exists, so both the repeated e1 and a new event with a different id record nothing.
Item 11 asks whether events run one at a time. Its pick queues events per handler, so two deliveries at the same time run in turn. The second one sees the existing release and records nothing.
Item 11 also asks what happens when the store fails. Its pick rejects that call and saves state only after set succeeds, so nothing is recorded and a retry succeeds.
